This is the whole of the starter's [`index.qmd`](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/starter/index.qmd), with each cell explained. Read it once and every other page will look familiar: a panel of inputs, a cell or two of computation, a chart block.

## The page

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
VM = window.VM
```

::: {.ojs-panel .ojs-row}
```{ojs}
viewof fText = Inputs.text({label: "f(x)", value: "sin(x) + x/3"})
```
```{ojs}
viewof k = Inputs.range([1, 5], {label: "Frequency", step: 0.1, value: 1})
```
:::

::: {.ojs-chart-block}
```{ojs}
vmTheme = Generators.observe(notify => VM.plotting.onThemeChange(notify))
chartColors = VM.plotting.colors(vmTheme)
```
```{ojs}
mainPlot = {
  const f = VM.expressions.makeFunction(math, fText)
  const xs = [], ys = []
  for (let i = 0; i <= 400; i++) {
    const x = -6 + 12 * i / 400
    xs.push(x)
    ys.push(f ? f(k * x) : NaN)
  }
  const div = document.createElement("div")
  div.className = "plotly-box-large"
  Plotly.newPlot(div, [
    {x: xs, y: ys, mode: "lines", name: fText, line: {color: chartColors.fn, width: 2.5}, showlegend: false}
  ], VM.plotting.layout({
    xaxis: {title: "x"},
    yaxis: {title: "f(kx)"},
    annotations: f ? [] : VM.plotting.emptyState("Couldn't parse that expression")
  }), VM.plotting.config())
  VM.plotting.autoResize(div)
  return div
}
```
:::

Type something unparseable into the field. Toggle the theme. Press ▶ on the slider.

## Cell by cell

### The panel

````markdown
::: {.ojs-panel .ojs-row}
```{ojs}
viewof fText = Inputs.text({label: "f(x)", value: "sin(x) + x/3"})
```
```{ojs}
viewof k = Inputs.range([1, 5], {label: "Frequency", step: 0.1, value: 1})
```
:::
````

A Quarto div with two classes around ordinary Observable inputs. `ojs-panel` is the look -- border, background, consistent input styling; `ojs-row` is the layout -- one wrapping row, the first control stretching to fill. The slider gets its play button for free. All the classes are on the [Markup](markup.qmd) page.

### The theme pair

```js
vmTheme = Generators.observe(notify => VM.plotting.onThemeChange(notify))
chartColors = VM.plotting.colors(vmTheme)
```

Put these two lines on every chart page. `chartColors` is the palette -- `chartColors.fn`, `.alt`, `.ok`, … -- and it changes when the reader toggles light/dark, so every cell that reads it redraws with the right colors. Without them, the chart's axes follow the toggle but your traces keep their old colors. (Why that is, and why `colors` takes an argument it ignores: [`onThemeChange`](reference/plotting.qmd#onThemeChange).)

### The function

```js
const f = VM.expressions.makeFunction(math, fText)
```

`math` is the math.js global the extension loaded. `makeFunction` turns the typed text into a JavaScript function, or gives **`null`** if it won't parse -- it never throws, so a half-typed expression can't break the page. Where evaluation fails (`sqrt(x)` at `x = -1`) the function gives `NaN`, which Plotly draws as a gap.

### The sampling loop

```js
for (let i = 0; i <= 400; i++) {
  const x = -6 + 12 * i / 400
  xs.push(x)
  ys.push(f ? f(k * x) : NaN)
}
```

A plain loop filling `xs` and `ys`. For a probability density, [`sampleCurve`](reference/distributions.qmd#sampleCurve) does this for you.

### The chart

```js
const div = document.createElement("div")
div.className = "plotly-box-large"
Plotly.newPlot(div, [...], VM.plotting.layout({...}), VM.plotting.config())
VM.plotting.autoResize(div)
return div
```

Make a `div`, draw into it, return it. Three library calls: [`layout()`](reference/plotting.qmd#layout) gives the themed layout with your own axis titles merged in, [`config()`](reference/plotting.qmd#config) the sensible Plotly config, and [`autoResize()`](reference/plotting.qmd#autoResize) sizes the chart once it's on the page. `plotly-box-large` is the one size class shipped -- full width, tall; set `div.style.height` for anything else.

### The empty state

```js
annotations: f ? [] : VM.plotting.emptyState("Couldn't parse that expression")
```

When `f` is `null` the chart would be an empty grid, indistinguishable from a valid function that's off-screen. [`emptyState`](reference/plotting.qmd#emptyState) puts a message in the middle so the reader knows it's their input.

### The chart block

````markdown
::: {.ojs-chart-block}
...
:::
````

The wrapper around the chart cells. It's what the fullscreen button enlarges, and where a floating legend or a slider bar attaches. Every chart wants one, even a chart with neither today, so that adding them later is just dropping in a cell.

## Where to go from here

Each of the starter's other pages adds one thing to this pattern:

| Page | Adds |
|---|---|
| [function-explorer.qmd](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/starter/function-explorer.qmd) | a floating legend ([`legendOverlay`](reference/ui.qmd#legendOverlay)); a field that turns red on bad input |
| [step-slider.qmd](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/starter/step-slider.qmd) | an iteration slider above the chart ([`ojs-chart-controls`](markup.qmd#ojs-chart-controls)) with playback; a results table |
| [ode-convergence.qmd](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/starter/ode-convergence.qmd) | ODE steppers; a Plotly chart and an Observable Plot chart sharing the theme |
| [distribution-explorer.qmd](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/starter/distribution-explorer.qmd) | an exact density over a histogram of seeded samples |
| [try-an-example.qmd](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/starter/try-an-example.qmd) | presets that fill the fields and run the page |
| [observable-plot.qmd](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz/blob/main/starter/observable-plot.qmd) | Observable Plot with a fullscreen button |

Then make the palette yours: [Theming](theming.qmd).
